name: Jahseja
title: One of Ezra's opponents in the matter of foreign marriages
summary: Jahseja was one of four men who opposed Ezra's command that the Israelites separate from their foreign wives after returning from exile in Babylon. He is mentioned in Ezra 10:15 as someone who resisted this arrangement.

keyEvents.title: Opposition to Ezra's marriage decree
keyEvents.description: Jahseja was one of four men appointed to stand against Ezra's ruling that the returned Jews should send away their foreign wives.

keyEvents.title: Ezra's reforms after the return
keyEvents.description: After returning from Babylon, Ezra introduced strict reforms to preserve the religious purity of the people, including the command to separate from foreign wives.

keyEvents.title: The assembly of the people in Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: All men of Judah and Benjamin were summoned to Jerusalem within three days to decide on the issue of foreign marriages.

keyEvents.title: Investigative Commission Established
keyEvents.description: A commission was established to investigate the cases of mixed marriages, and the work was completed by the first day of the first month.
